sentences.text: Gadi Eisenkot has vowed to oust Benjamin Netanyahu, but still has to get enough parties on board Israel's new parliament will be sworn in on Tuesday, as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot seeks to oust caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: The former army chief was tasked with forming a government by the president, after he received the backing of 67 members of the 120-seat Knesset, compared to 46 for Netanyahu.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: But Eisenkot faces an uphill struggle.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: His bloc of four parties won 48 seats in last month's election, while Netanyahu's bloc won 53, leaving both short of a majority.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: He has 28 days to build a coalition, with a possible two-week extension.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: Almost half of the MKs being sworn in did not serve in the previous parliament, while Arab-led parties have a record number of seats.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: The outcome of the election, which was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu, means there is a period of uncertainty over who will form the next government.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: Netanyahu will remain caretaker prime minister until then - a process which could take from days to months.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: One of the most dramatic results was the performance of Israel's two Arab-led alliances - the United Arab List and the Joint List - which won an unprecedented 19 seats between them following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: The Arab parties could therefore hold the balance of power, although Netanyahu has ruled out governing with them and three of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc have opposed including them in a coalition.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: On Sunday, President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with trying to form a government.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: Speaking at the president's residence, the centrist Yashar party leader called for the formation of a "national emergency government" - an implicit appeal to parties to put ideological differences aside to remove Netanyahu from office.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: This, he said, would "require creative and unconventional political steps".
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: Eisenkot said any party or MK prepared to accept four principles could join his proposed government.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: The four requirements, however, could present significant obstacles to Eisenkot's potential partners.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: The conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jewish men, who are exempt from military service if they are in full-time religious study, was a major election issue.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: The ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism (UTJ) and Shas parties, which won 13 seats in total, have fiercely objected to attempts to change the status quo - something that all parties in Eisenkot's bloc campaigned to do.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: Eisenkot's four principles are also contentious for the Arab parties.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: Both emphasise equal national and civic rights for Israel's Arab citizens, who form about 20% of the population; the vast majority of Israeli Arabs are not required to serve in the military; and neither has publicly recognised Hamas as a terrorist organisation.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: The Arab parties could, though, help Eisenkot form a minority government.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: The United Arab List, which won eight seats, has said it is willing to be part of an Eisenkot-led coalition, while the Joint List, which won 11 seats, has offered parliamentary support from the outside.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: If Eisenkot accepted such an arrangement, he would still have to persuade other parties in his bloc to agree.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: Avigdor Lieberman, whose Yisrael Beiteinu party won seven seats, has so far refused to join a minority government dependent on Arab MKs.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: In return for their support, the ultra-Orthodox parties would be likely to demand major concessions on military conscription, which might be unacceptable to most of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: Netanyahu - Israel's longest-serving leader - reiterated in a video on Monday his call for the formation of a government of national unity, which he said he would lead as prime minister.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: He said any Zionist party - those which support Israel as a Jewish state - including opposition parties, would be eligible.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: He warned against a government which relied on what he called "the Islamists", an apparent reference to Arab parties.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: "You cannot form a government with Hamas supporters," he said.
sentences.article_title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government

sentences.text: Sales of essential goods such as bottled water and canned food soared in the 10 days following the launch of the government's "Be Ready" emergency preparedness campaign on 22 October, research indicates.
sentences.article_title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator.
sentences.article_title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: The government's public awareness campaign encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.
sentences.article_title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.
sentences.article_title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days-worth of food and water in their homes.
sentences.article_title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: Wet wipes, a torch and cash were also recommended.
sentences.article_title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: After the campaign launch, the equivalent of an extra 400,000 people per day bought tinned meat, Worldpanel said, although the typical amount remained at 500g, which suggests a gradual stocking-up.
sentences.article_title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: "Shoppers clearly took notice of the 'Be Ready' campaign, but this wasn't panic buying, with less than a third of households buying bottled water in October," said Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel by Numerator.
sentences.article_title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: "Growth came from more people adding the recommended items on the government's checklist to their weekly shop, not from shoppers piling their trolleys high, which is very much in line with what the government wanted households to do," he said.
sentences.article_title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: Further evidence of stockpiling came from food firm Princes on Tuesday, which said demand for tinned tuna, meat and vegetables had risen following the government's campaign.
sentences.article_title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: Princes interim chief executive Giuseppe Mastrolia said the jump in demand "further reinforces the relevance of our core categories in providing affordable, nutritious and convenient food solutions".
sentences.article_title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: The "Be Ready" campaign warns that severe weather and cyber attacks could disrupt essential services, and British households need to make sure they have what they need - for example, bottled water, and long-life food that doesn't need to be kept in the fridge such as dried fruit and nuts.
sentences.article_title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said everyone should have "those supplies in the house to get you through those moments".

sentences.text: One big series that's hoping to help change that is Football Manager - the popular simulation that puts players in charge of their own team.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: The latest edition of the annual franchise allows people to use the game's custom character designer to create a manager who uses a wheelchair.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: Developer Sports Interactive tells BBC Newsbeat it's part of wider efforts to make the game "as inclusive as possible".
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: You can now design a character who uses a wheelchair in Football Manager In a 2023 survey , external of gamers with disabilities by charity Scope, respondents said their top priorities included more accurate and more frequent representation in games.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: Will Rees, a gamer and powerchair football player for Wrexham, says it's "amazing" to see the new feature in Football Manager.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: "I probably might play it more even though I'm not good at it," says, Will, 16.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: "More wheelchair users will feel more included." Notable video game characters with disabilities include Hailey Cooper, Miles Morales' love interest in the Spider-Man games, who is deaf and communicates using American Sign Language.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: In Grand Theft Auto 5, heist mastermind Lester uses a walking stick and a wheelchair.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: Will, who has kyphosis (curvature of the spine) and other conditions affecting his joints, says he can see where it would be difficult for certain video games to include disabled representation.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: But he hopes it becomes more standard in future.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: "We just want to be like everyone else.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: We don't want to be someone else or be treated differently," he says.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: Grand Theft Auto's heist mastermind Lester uses a walking stick and a wheelchair Sports Interactive's head of production Stu Boyd says introducing wheelchairs is "step two" in the company's representation plan after it added hearing aids and eye patches in 2025.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: "We can't do everything in one year," he says.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: "So we just have to keep doing it every year to try and get to that gold standard in the future." Where representation is concerned, Boyd says, "it's really important that it suits the game".
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: Character artist Steve Norgate says the work to add wheelchair users "took a little while" because it's important to "do everything 100% right".
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: The Football Manager team also changed elements of the in-game world to reflect the needs of wheelchair users, such as adding ramps to trophy plinths.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: Accessibility website Can I Play That? , external said it was a "a lovely example of going beyond just representation, and thinking about inclusion as well".
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: It also noted accessibility improvements to the game, such as reducing the number of clicks required to navigate its menus, and the ability to customise the way information is displayed.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: Producer Danny Quin says they also had to change things such as camera angles and how the manager acts on the side of the pitch when matches play out.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: "Now we've done that," he says, "we are in a place to be able to do a lot more".
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: Boyd says it comes down to striking a balance between the team's finite resources and the features they'd like to add, but that the positive reaction online will "feed the team and feed our decisions going forwards".
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: While there was big praise for Football Manager's latest inclusion, the announcement of the new feature did attract some negative comments online.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: "Once that representation becomes normal and more people do it, then we might not see as much reaction to it," says Boyd.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: "Hopefully that'll be a more positive landscape for the gaming industry." Worthing FC owner George Dowell MBE, who has a spinal cord injury, says "silly comments" are often to be expected.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: "Hopefully changes like this will bring more people in wheelchairs into football," he says.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: "Nothing will ever change if you don't change anything".
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: "If you can see yourself you might think: 'Okay I'm really loving managing this.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: I want to go and try this in real life'.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: "I know in the last few years, [developers] have been working hard to make the games more accessible for people to actually play them, which has been great.
sentences.article_title: Football Manager series shines a light on video game representation

sentences.text: "The next step is to see ourselves fully in those games." Listen to Newsbeat live at 12:45 and 17:45 weekdays - or listen back here .

sentences.text: Rimini (l) and Sienna Chapman were celebrating a friend's 21st in Krakow when the attack happened Twin sisters who were in Krakow when a gunman killed six people have told how they "ran for our lives" when they heard shots.
sentences.article_title: Twins 'ran for our lives' as Krakow attack unfolded

sentences.text: Sienna and Rimini Chapman, 20, from Northallerton, North Yorkshire, were part of a group celebrating a friend's 21st birthday in Poland when gunfire sounded in the city's Main Market Square at about 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) on Saturday.
sentences.article_title: Twins 'ran for our lives' as Krakow attack unfolded

sentences.text: The 24-year-old attacker, who died in hospital on Monday, fatally shot four Polish citizens, a British national and an Austrian woman, while a further 15 people, including two police officers, were injured.
sentences.article_title: Twins 'ran for our lives' as Krakow attack unfolded

sentences.text: Sienna told the BBC their experiences during the attack had been "terrifying".
sentences.article_title: Twins 'ran for our lives' as Krakow attack unfolded

sentences.text: The group of friends were walking towards a cafe in the square when they first heard gunfire.
sentences.article_title: Twins 'ran for our lives' as Krakow attack unfolded

sentences.text: "At first I thought the shots were to scare the pigeons away, but then everyone suddenly started running towards us," Sienna said.
sentences.article_title: Twins 'ran for our lives' as Krakow attack unfolded

sentences.text: Staff and other customers inside the cafe had not heard gunfire and were "carrying on as normal", Rimini said.
sentences.article_title: Twins 'ran for our lives' as Krakow attack unfolded

sentences.text: She added: "Everyone else was completely oblivious.
sentences.article_title: Twins 'ran for our lives' as Krakow attack unfolded

sentences.text: It was like we were in two different worlds where we had heard the shots but other people weren't aware.
sentences.article_title: Twins 'ran for our lives' as Krakow attack unfolded

sentences.text: "We were telling the staff to lock the doors, but I don't think they understood what we were saying because of the language barrier.
sentences.article_title: Twins 'ran for our lives' as Krakow attack unfolded

sentences.text: "After a few minutes though they did lock the doors." The sisters, originally from Worcester, said they took shelter under tables and stayed there for two hours while keeping in touch with family members and following BBC News updates about the attack online.
sentences.article_title: Twins 'ran for our lives' as Krakow attack unfolded

sentences.text: The twin sisters said they were left "extremely shaken" by the experience Sienna added: "We eventually felt safe enough to leave and return to our nearby hotel, where we stayed for the rest of the evening.
sentences.article_title: Twins 'ran for our lives' as Krakow attack unfolded

sentences.text: "The whole experience was terrifying, we were extremely shaken by what had happened." Rimini said the group had initially planned to have a meal out to celebrate Millie's birthday on Saturday evening but later focused on returning to the UK following the attack.

sentences.text: Prince William carried out his own fact-finding meetings with service women The Prince of Wales says more must be done to ensure that women in the armed forces are shown respect and protected from sexual harassment.
sentences.article_title: Prince William wants more protection from harassment for service women

sentences.text: Prince William has called for a military culture that is more inclusive and respectful of women - and has warned that at present those values are not always being met.
sentences.article_title: Prince William wants more protection from harassment for service women

sentences.text: The prince, who will one day be head of the armed forces, held private meetings with service women for an article he has produced as guest editor of Country Life magazine.
sentences.article_title: Prince William wants more protection from harassment for service women

sentences.text: He was told about service women too often facing inappropriate comments, the threat of false rumours and sexual harassment.
sentences.article_title: Prince William wants more protection from harassment for service women

sentences.text: He has now raised some of those concerns about the issues concerning women in the armed forces, in the article he commissioned for Country Life.
sentences.article_title: Prince William wants more protection from harassment for service women

sentences.text: It cites a survey from the Ministry of Defence that found 67% of service women had faced unwanted "sexualised behaviour" every year and that 30% had considered leaving the armed forces because of such behaviour.
sentences.article_title: Prince William wants more protection from harassment for service women

sentences.text: The article also references the experiences of Royal Artillery Gunner Jaysley Beck, who took her own life at Larkhill Camp in Wiltshire in 2021.
sentences.article_title: Prince William wants more protection from harassment for service women

sentences.text: Gunner Beck had faced months of unwanted attention and had reported a sexual assault and an inquest heard about a complaints system that failed to adequately respond.
sentences.article_title: Prince William wants more protection from harassment for service women

sentences.text: Earlier this year, four young women told the BBC they were sexually assaulted and harassed at an Army training college for teenagers - the Army Foundation College at Harrogate, North Yorkshire - with one saying she was raped by fellow junior soldiers in an attack that lasted hours.

sentences.article_title: Prince William wants more protection from harassment for service women

sentences.text: One-flowered wintergreens are only found in woodlands in north-east Scotland Conservationists say thousands of rare flowers have been saved from falling into the sea on the Moray coast.
sentences.article_title: Patch of one of UK's rarest flowers saved from falling into the sea

sentences.text: In the UK, the one-flowered wintergreen can only be found in pine woodlands in north-east Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Patch of one of UK's rarest flowers saved from falling into the sea

sentences.text: More than half the entire population of the star-shaped flower have been lost over the last 50 years.
sentences.article_title: Patch of one of UK's rarest flowers saved from falling into the sea

sentences.text: About 3,400 of the tiny plants have been rescued from an area of eroded beach at Culbin Sands, an area of dunes and forest near Findhorn, and moved to a safe location nearby.

sentences.text: A patch of the flowers was carefully dug up at a site on the coast where it has been eroded away by the sea over the last few years.
sentences.article_title: Patch of one of UK's rarest flowers saved from falling into the sea

sentences.text: Sam Jones, senior ecological adviser at Plantlife Scotland, said: "This type of ground-breaking conservation work will help ensure endangered species like the one-flowered wintergreen are not lost.

sentences.text: Instead of relying on photosynthesis - a process involving sunlight, water and carbon dioxide - to create food and oxygen to survive, the flowers can also take energy from fungus in woodland soils.
sentences.article_title: Patch of one of UK's rarest flowers saved from falling into the sea

sentences.text: Conservationists said increasingly warmer conditions caused by climate change risked drying up these damp soils.
sentences.article_title: Patch of one of UK's rarest flowers saved from falling into the sea

sentences.text: Iain Macdonald, biodiversity adviser at NatureScot said: "We don't yet know how many plants will survive at their new home in Culbin Forest.
sentences.article_title: Patch of one of UK's rarest flowers saved from falling into the sea

sentences.text: "But we do know that it was only a matter of time before they would have all been lost to the sea if we'd left them where they were.
sentences.article_title: Patch of one of UK's rarest flowers saved from falling into the sea

sentences.text: "So, any survival will be a success, and if we can continue to introduce more plants to some of the small, existing populations then we'll strengthen their ability to cope with our changing environment." sentences.text: Under the ZEV mandate, the percentage of new car sales that need to be EVs increases each year.

sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: A jet engine will have hundreds of turbine blades Every time you fly, an extraordinary feat of endurance occurs inside the aircraft's engines.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Hidden from view inside the sleek outer nacelle are hundreds of little turbine blades that can shrug off enormous mechanical stresses and temperatures exceeding 1,500C.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: It is a true engineering marvel.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And these hardy blades are not sculpted or cut from their material – they are grown.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: During the 1960s, engineers worked out how to take a molten metal alloy, cast it into the shape of a turbine blade, and then cool it very carefully from one end to the other over a matter of hours.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A single crystal or grain of metal alloy forms during this process of gradual, delicate solidification.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Like turning a cup of water into one big snowflake, of your own design, rather than a mini blizzard of many smaller snowflakes.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "It's about as complicated as manufacturing gets," says Ben Fifoot, manufacturing engineer at Rolls-Royce, which makes turbine blades in the UK.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "It's a real motivator to get out of bed in the morning." Only a handful of companies around the world can produce these single crystal turbine blades, and the process has been perfected end-to-end in just five countries, including the US and UK.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Engine-makers continually vie for access to the technology.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Rolls-Royce, GE and France's Safran are among the few firms that have perfected the process.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: In September, GE Aerospace announced , external it would acquire its turbine blade supplier for $11.75bn (£8.78bn).
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Neither company responded to BBC News' requests for comment but the move has been described as an effort to ensure supply of these critical components.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Separately, in March, Rolls-Royce said it would invest more than £19m in its Rotherham blade casting facility.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Turbine blade specialists continue to work on improving the capabilities of this little-known technology.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: All the while, China is desperate to prove that its engineers can produce turbine blades of the same quality as those in the West.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Who will come out on top?
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "Demand for [turbine blades] is huge.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: So few companies have managed to do it, which does give it this kind of magical aura," says Bill Sweetman, an aviation industry writer and consultant.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: He suspects GE Aerospace's recent move is about securing reliability and predictability in the notoriously volatile aircraft manufacturing supply chain.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The casts play a crucial part in the cooling process But why is the single crystal casting process, which has been around for decades now, still so specialist?
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: To grow one of these blades, asserts Fifoot, is to "fight the laws of the universe".
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: This is because each molten blade would naturally cool into a solid object consisting of many small grains of metal alloy, all jumbled together.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: But you don't want a crumbly sugar cube, you want a perfect diamond.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Getting a single crystal to grow into the shape of the blade instead isn't just a matter of cooling the molten version down slowly, the process also uses a bizarre trick called a pigtail.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The pigtail is a small spiral at one end of the blade.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Fifoot says that, at the beginning of the cooling process, this spiral "chokes" the flow of solidifying crystals so that just one takes over.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A bit like a hairpin corner in an F1 race right before the finish line – one driver can take the lead here and go on to win.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "Sometimes we need to play around with the number of turns or the angles on [the pigtail] to try and get more favourable grain," adds Fifoot.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Once the blade is formed, this crucial but sacrificial spiral is cut off.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: France's Safran is among the few companies that can make single crystal blades Blades made by Rolls-Royce are used in aircraft engines including the Trent XWB-84, which powers the Airbus A350-900, and the Trent 1000 XE, for the Boeing 787.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The single crystal is essential to ensure each blade's performance.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Sometimes a blade doesn't cool quite as planned, for example two crystals form within it instead of just one, and the metal alloy must be reprocessed so that the manufacturer may re-use the material.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Special ceramic coatings also protect blades from extreme temperatures inside engines.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And another important feature is that blades are cast with tiny channels that allow a flow of cooler air to coat them in a kind of film while the aircraft engine is working.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "The drive at the moment [across the industry] is currently to make those cooling passages really intricate," says Paul Withey, at the University of Birmingham, who formerly worked for Rolls-Royce.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The more turbulent those little flows of cool air are, he explains, the more they will knock heat out of the surrounding, much hotter air.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And blade-makers also seek to reduce the mass of these components as much as possible.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "If we can take any weight out of it, you can run that engine more efficiently using less fuel – you can spin it faster and hotter," says Fifoot.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The turbine blades are used in the Trent 1000 engine among others Meanwhile, China hopes to become only the sixth country to master the whole technology chain for single crystal blade casting.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A report in May , external quoted one engineer at the AECC Beijing Institute of Aeronautical Materials claiming that China now had a single crystal alloy "superior to or equivalent to the second-generation single-crystal superalloys widely used in Europe and the US".
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: It costs less to make, too, apparently.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: But the West has a "huge advantage" over China given that the majority of commercial airliner production happens there, says Sweetman.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Supply chains and the latest innovations are generally clustered in the West.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Plus, Western manufacturers also have lengthy safety records under their belts.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: China must compete on practically every aspect of aircraft manufacturing , external – by no means just on turbine blades – in order to make serious in-roads.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "You can definitely see that happening but it's a long, uphill struggle," adds Sweetman.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Demand for aircraft is currently high, which is already straining various supply chains in the industry.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: That demand could grow higher still, suggests Withey.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: During the next few years, one of the two main aircraft manufacturers, Airbus and Boeing, could launch a new short-haul plane , external , he says.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Then, the other would have to follow suit in order to remain competitive.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "There'll be a bun fight," says Withey, over who gets to supply the engines and, by extension, those all-important single crystal turbine blades. sentences.text: Managing AI agents is a big part of Lotte Underwood's job Recent university graduate Lotte Underwood is a public relations executive with a twist - she spends more time using AI than actually doing PR.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Underwood, 25, joined London-based PR agency Fight or Flight in November last year, in the new role of "AI associate" after completing a degree and then a masters in marketing.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: She's part of a recently established, dedicated AI team that has built around 30 AI agents.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Specific tasks include industry research, client reporting, media interview preparation, helping clients create clearer briefs, and image generation.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: A big part of Underwood's job is to manage those agents, check their outputs and feed those to the team members who are dealing directly with clients and the media.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Another key responsibility of hers is to monitor how clients appear in the responses from AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and others.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "A huge part is being in client meetings and calls to work out what is actually going to be most helpful from these agents," says Underwood.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: AI is seen as one of the main factors behind graduate job cuts , but companies are also creating dedicated AI-specific graduate roles like Underwood's.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Dillan Patel, for example, joined engineering software company Stride 18 months ago as an intern.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: A business management graduate, he was put to work developing an internal chatbot designed to capture the knowledge of a senior staff member transitioning into retirement.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Patel, 24, is now an AI automation analyst, tasked with developing further internal agents to provide specific information to individual teams, while also identifying which manual or repetitive tasks across the company could be done by AI.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "My role focuses on finding practical ways to use technology, automation, data and AI to improve how we operate," says Coventry-based Patel.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Debra Maxwell is looking for "AI disruptors" Such AI savvy graduates are also in demand from companies like ArvatoConnect, an outsourced contact centre company.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: CEO Debra Maxwell says the company's usual graduate intake is on hold this year, but she plans to resume it next year with a bigger focus on AI.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We would be looking for more AI-disruptor type roles, where you can challenge us as an organisation to think more holistically about where AI can be applied and where we could grow our business from," says London-based Maxwell.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We see our graduates as not filling administrative roles, but actually adding value to the organisation in a different way." Maxwell adds: "For example, one of our recent graduates is using AI to do deep dives on specific markets, and provide more information for when we're bidding [for new contracts].
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: It's basically giving him a more rounded role." If AI can make a graduate job bigger and more integral to the organisation, Maxwell argues that companies can create a more loyal, engaged workforce that is able to contribute more meaningfully, much earlier.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Research from consultancy PwC found that some graduate roles are assuming more responsibilities because of AI, as it allows companies to demand more senior abilities from junior hires.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: For the consultancy's 2026 AI Jobs Barometer , external , it analysed 2.4 million entry-level jobs in the US.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: It found that the entry-level roles most influenced by AI are now seven times more likely to require traditionally senior-level skills.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: These include motivational leadership, strategic decision making and team building.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Those entry-level roles with higher expectations have in fact grown 35% since 2019, PwC found, while other entry-level roles actually shrank by 10%.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Cian Clinton uses around ten AI agents for work tasks Cian Clinton, who joined consultancy Valliance last September after graduating from a Bachelor of Science in 2024, says the incorporation of AI into his role makes him feel less like a graduate, and more like an equal team member.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: He uses around 10 AI agents daily for different tasks.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "Your ideas and your creativity are a lot more valued because you actually get to implement those firsthand, and the responsibility you take on is a lot greater because of that," says London-based Clinton, 23.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "I am now taking on responsibilities which would usually take me four or five years to get to." His career progression, he believes, will now be faster as a result.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "AI is killing the 'pyramid' approach…progression is no longer based on your knowledge bank.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Now it's more based on your critical thinking and understanding of the processes," says Clinton.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: There's no doubt Underwood, Patel and Clinton are developing valuable AI knowledge which can help them across their careers.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: But with their time at work so focused on AI, does it matter how much - or how little - time they're spending learning about the professional field they're supposed to be operating in?
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Underwood says she'd like to still pick up the traditional PR skills her role isn't currently focused on, but is confident of her future in the agency's growing AI team.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "There's certain things that I haven't had the chance to do yet, like directly pitching to the media.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: I absolutely plan to do this," she says.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Graduates becoming too AI-centric is an issue for Simon Pratt, chief operating officer at Portman Finance Group.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: He says being able to use AI effectively is important, but the company's two-year graduate programme is fully centred on "learning the trade".
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "Our graduates rotate across four areas at six-month intervals, working directly alongside senior relationship managers to learn their trade," Northampton-based Pratt explains.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "They'll learn all of our financial products, how to draft credit papers for submission to lenders, and how to build meaningful relationships with our customers.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: They'll progress to running transactions from start to finish." Claire Reid, PwC UK's chief technology and innovation officer, believes graduate roles that are too AI heavy won't necessarily provide graduates long-term career progression.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "There will be no graduate job now that doesn't require a baseline of AI literacy," says Glasgow-based Reid.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "But AI skills on their own are not going to help you in your career.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: You've got to couple that with that sector knowledge of what that client actually wants." Back in Coventry, Dillan Patel is confident his AI work will continue to be valuable, and he wants to keep building on it.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "I don't think I'd want to explore different positions within the business.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Through my involvement in AI-related projects, I already work closely with different areas of the business and I'm gaining valuable knowledge and experience along the way," he says.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is often rated as one of the greatest video games The moment she saw footage from the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Kacey Doran picked up her phone.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: She had to tell her sister.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: "Have you seen this?" messaged Doran, excitedly.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Nearly 30 years ago, a 10-year-old Doran had sat in front of her family's TV, reading out the dialogue on screen to her sister, a year younger, as they inched their way through the original Nintendo 64 game's sprawling, puzzle-filled dungeons.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Ocarina's fantasy-like story, and beautiful music, enthralled them both.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: It was also the first game Doran ever completed.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Now, countless memories rushed back to her as she devoured clips of the fully redesigned version, due to arrive on the Switch 2 later this year.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Doran's sister messaged back: "I'm not tearing up… YOU'RE tearing up." News of a video game remake bought back happy memories for Kacey Doran This is the power of nostalgia – and a perfect example of how video games can trigger it.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Doran now teaches an esports course at Rowan University in New Jersey.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: She says the original Ocarina of Time, released in 1998, had a "magical" quality that she hopes to rediscover, and also share with her sister's children.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: The video games industry has long leaned on remakes.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: From Mario Kart to the Final Fantasy series, or even Pac-Man, some games just keep coming back in updated forms, as new generations of gamers emerge and as computer hardware improves, enabling more detailed graphics and increasingly expansive game worlds.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: While the emotional hook may be the most significant draw, putting out a remake can be a double-edged sword.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Some gamers are very protective of their favourite titles and new versions don't always meet certain fans' astronomically high expectations.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Nostalgia is an important but mixed emotion, says Tim Wulf, at the Centre for Advanced Internet Studies in Bochum, Germany.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: It has positive aspects but also a kind of sadness, too.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Happiness in remembering things that were important to us, and also an awareness that that time is now gone.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: "It's a social emotion because memories that induce nostalgia for us are connected to other people," he explains, adding that nostalgia can boost our self-esteem while highlighting key social bonds.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Video games, says Wulf, are notoriously good at triggering nostalgia because gamers can "jump into the same environment".
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: In other words, games are like time machines for our emotions, and returning to fondly remembered places can feel stabilising or reassuring in an ever-changing world.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Doran, for one, notes that when you return to a favourite old game, there's something satisfying about deploying previously learned skills.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: You know what to do here, you're winning again.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Video games are good at triggering nostalgic feelings says Tim Wulf Putting out remasters and remakes has been a "really successful" strategy for the games industry, says Piers Harding-Rolls, head of games research at Ampere Analysis.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: "Tying in with established audiences and building on existing content is quite a safe route for a lot of companies," he adds.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: In many cases, it is cheaper to update an existing game rather than create a new title from scratch.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Among other remakes that have found big audiences recently are those of Resident Evil 4 and Assassin's Creed Black Flag.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: But Ocarina of Time perhaps stands out because, ever since its original release, it has been considered by many as one of the greatest games ever made.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: "The interest from all the Gen Zs that I work with is really high," says Harding-Rolls.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: The legend of The Legend of Zelda, as it were.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Since 2007 there have been 14 main releases of Assassin's Creed Clearly, nostalgia is not the only driver of interest in the remake, and today's audiences will expect a game that plays to today's standards.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Games companies must keep innovating when linking contemporary audiences to the past, says Wulf, in order satisfy their desire for fresh experiences.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: And although Wulf himself was a big fan of the original, he has no personal interest in the Ocarina of Time remake.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: "I want a new game – I don't want to play an old game," he says.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Nostalgia isn't always enough for some.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Plus, critics often highlight a tension between originals and remakes.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Which is the definitive version?
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: In 2021, Square Enix released the bizarrely titled Nier Replicant ver.1.22474487139... – a remaster of a game first published in 2010.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: One reviewer wrote , external , "What we're left with is two nearly identical Niers each vying to be the true Nier." Fans may react badly should a remaster or remake fail to do justice to the source material.

sentences.text: And, in the gaming world, angry fan reactions can be serious .

sentences.text: Amazon Prime Air is expanding to 500 US towns and cities Nature lover Ashley Schmidt no longer spends much time in her garden, in the Dallas suburb of North Garland.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It's all because she can't stand the sound of the delivery drones that fly overhead, depositing her neighbours' online orders.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "They emit this very annoying buzz.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It triggers my fight or flight response," says the 44-year-old administrative assistant.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "You can hear the drones on approach and you can hear them inside your home when they pass directly overhead and then you hear them as they leave," she says.

sentences.text: Amazon says it is working to reduce the noise of its drone fleet Schmidt is one of a growing number of people living with the noise of drones dispatched by companies including Amazon and Walmart as they seek to speed up home deliveries.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Delivery drone services, not long ago a novelty, are becoming part of everyday life for many people in the US.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Among them, Amazon Prime Air is in the process of expanding deliveries to nearly 500 cities and towns, delivering items that fit into a space the size of a shoe box.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It has also launched to customers in and around Darlington in the north of England.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Smaller drone delivery services are popping up too: in some US cities, customers can order flying treats from their local pizza joint or ice cream parlour.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Even in cities where noise is already a steady part of life, the sound of drones seems to irk in a particular way.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: While the steady passing of traffic might blend into the background, the sudden whine of a drone's rotors can pierce the everyday hum.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The sound tends to be "particularly noticeable, even when overall sound levels are relatively low," says Antonio Torija Martinez, professor in acoustic engineering and psychoacoustics at the University of Salford.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Unlike planes, drones operate at low altitudes and may fly directly over residential areas.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "They can expose communities that have not previously experienced significant aircraft noise, and who may therefore be more sensitive to changes in their local soundscape," says Torija Martinez.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: He points to research showing that people respond strongly to a noise when they consider the source to be "novel, intrusive or frequent".
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: People who benefit from a drone delivery service, for example, may be less bothered by the noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The FAA says operators and local community leaders have primary responsibility for addressing any community concerns.

sentences.text: The London-based business has designed a propulsion system it claims can reduce drone noise by at least two thirds.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Its system also quietens things down through slower rotor speed and by using materials that reduce vibration noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Greenjets' low-noise tech has been used by police and harbour security teams in Germany.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "There are some efforts to reduce the sound of drones.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "Make it faster, not less quiet, seems to be the approach," says Tollast.

sentences.text: Sharrow Engineering developed twisted propellers that reduce noise For Detroit-based entrepreneur, Greg Sharrow, it was the challenge of broadcasting a classical music performance back in 2012 that set him on the path to quieter drone design.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: He needed to film a violinist from a tricky angle and a drone seemed the only solution – except that it would be far too noisy.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: As a starting point, "I knew that most of the noise from the drone was coming from the propeller, not the motor," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Specifically, it was the tips of the blades that he realised were creating the noise as they swiped through the air.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "I asked myself a very simple question, what would a tipless propeller look like and how would it function?" The result was to create a propeller with twisted loop-shaped blades with no points.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It turned out it was easier to test his propeller in water than it was to repeatedly fly a drone, which led Sharrow to initially develop a less noisy boat propeller.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Now, however, his company, Sharrow Engineering, is focusing on developing "ultra-quiet" drone rotors.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "We have validated that the technology works in drone applications and that it is dramatically quieter," says Sharrow.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Companies at the forefront of drone deliveries say they are also working to reduce the noise of their fleets.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: A spokesperson for Amazon says it has made "measurable sound improvements" to its drones and its latest designs use custom-designed propellers "that produce almost half the perceived sound of the prior generation, with a milder tone".
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Drone maker Wing, which provides its vehicles for Walmart deliveries, says its propellers are designed to minimise noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It also varies its flight paths to prevent repeated overflights over any single home or neighbourhood.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Mohammed Ashim is paid to film his hands at work Mohammed Ashim has been cutting hair and trimming beards for four years in Bengaluru.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: But recently the 22-year old has been strapping a camera to his head to record his work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The camera only records his hands and fingers - his client's faces are blurred out.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "The routine is simple, but you have to be disciplined about how you move.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The operations team taught me that my hands always have to stay cleanly inside the frame, the lighting has to be sharp, and I can't tilt my head too abruptly while working." He wears the camera for five or six hours a day.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "It's good money, but honestly, the feeling of doing something this futuristic is what keeps me excited.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: I never imagined my razor techniques would be useful to a global tech company," says Ashim.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: He is one of hundreds of thousands of workers across the world paid to record their activities.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Ashim's footage is collected by a local company, which might have hundreds of people filming their work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: That video is then sold on to technology companies and research organisations who use it to train artificial intelligence - in particular so-called physical AI, a type of artificial intelligence that can control robots in the real world.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Rashdan Technologies collects and processes such human generated data.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Every robotics company, every frontier AI lab, has a specific kind of data they want: industrial tasks, agriculture, household chores, small business work like pottery, garment-making, embroidery, candle-making.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We go wherever the task is," says co-founder and CEO Shahil Baig.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: His company pays $5 to $10 (£3.74; £7.47) for eight to 10 hours of recorded work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "For a lot of these people, that's meaningful," Baig says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Making sure workers give their consent and are comfortable with the process is important, he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "We record hands, not faces, and where multi-camera rigs do capture more of the body or environment, we blur faces out.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: No names, no contact details, nothing that identifies them personally goes into what we hand off." But his customers are getting more demanding.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Now clients are asking for four to six cameras rigged around a person's head to cover the entire scene, not just the hands.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Getting someone to agree to one small camera is one conversation.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Getting them to agree to wearing what's effectively a five-camera headset is a completely different, and harder, one.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We pay more for that tier of data collection because of what we're asking of people." And the industry is becoming more crowded, Agarwal expects dozens more competitors to emerge in India this year.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Shahil Baig expects dozens more firms to start collecting video of workers Why is such data so important?
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: If you want robots to navigate the real world, they can't just be trained inside computer simulations, argues Manish Agarwal, the founder of Humyn Labs, which collects and processes human-generated data.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Most of that data comes from video, but sometimes collectors wear hardware on their hands and fingers to capture physical contact.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Physical tasks require high-quality signals involving limb movements, fingers, wrists, elbows, shoulders and dynamic force application.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: For example: applying the correct grip force so a plastic bottle doesn't crumble versus a steel glass," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: And until recently, that data was not available.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "There is no existing internet archive of embodied human activity - no dataset of a kitchen being cleaned, or a car being assembled by hands that know exactly how much force to apply.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: That data has to be captured from scratch, in the real world, across diverse environments," says Agarwal, whose company has bases in Bangalore and San Francisco.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: At the moment his firm has 96,000 data collectors across countries in Latin America and Southeast Asia.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Humyn Labs filters the thousands of hours of video supplied by those collectors, selecting the most useful content.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: It's then labelled so the AI knows what it is looking at and packaged in a format that can be used by clients.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "You need to source across a variety of factories, a variety of tasks, in different geographies because if you want to build deployment for US factories or US houses, you'd want environments that are a proxy for that.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Residential houses in India may not be the right context for building a robotics use case for the US." This video can not be played The factory workers teaching robots how to work like humans But are workers collecting data for machines that will one day do their jobs?
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: At the moment it's too early to tell says Bino Paul, senior professor at the School of Management and Labour Studies at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) in Mumbai.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: For some workers AI might be a useful tool, but robots could automate other jobs, he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The problem is that, if machines do start to take over, there will be little workers can do about.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "By the time workers realise what they have participated in, things may have gone too far," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Like many others, he wants governments to regulate AI.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "AI cannot be viewed merely as a technical system.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We need to develop a socio-technical system in which ethics is upheld through human agency, ensuring that AI delivers beneficence rather than maleficence." Despite concerns over where AI is heading, money is still being poured into its development.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Some of that trickles down to workers in India, where there is no shortage of workers prepared to wear a camera for a few dollars a day.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Mohammed Arman has been working in the textiles industry in Bangalore for 10 years.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Garments stitching and cutting.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: I know this work so well I could probably do it with my eyes closed.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Cloth, thread, needle, machine after 10 years, your hands just know what to do before your mind even tells them," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: He has recently started wearing a head-mounted camera that records his work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: I have a family back home in Bihar, and every rupee I send back matters.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: If someone offers me extra money to wear a camera while I do the exact same work I've been doing for 10 years, I'm not going to say no.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "It doesn't cost me anything.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: I'm already doing the stitching, already doing the cutting.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Now I just get paid a little more for it," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Mohammed Arman has been filming his tailoring work While there is demand for such footage it will be collected somewhere.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "India's current role in this industry is largely as a supplier of raw material - people strap on cameras, record themselves doing ordinary tasks, and that footage gets shipped off to labs abroad," Agarwal says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: But he argues the value of that kind of work will quickly become eroded, as more companies compete for collection contracts.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "India can't afford to stay a footage supplier.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: It needs to move up the value chain: from recording raw video to owning the pipeline that turns that video into something usable - cleaning it, structuring it, validating it, and ultimately setting the standards for what counts as high-quality training data," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI
