sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered to take action over odours Milpitas, an affluent city in California's Silicon Valley tech hub, has an odour problem.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: For decades, residents have had to endure rank smells wafting from industrial sites, among them a 342-acre landfill.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "When I first moved here, I could not open my window for over 10 years," says Chia-Ling Kong, an engineer for a tech firm who lives around half a mile from the dump.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: While things have got better in recent years, Kong says she and her neighbours must still contend with around "two or three hours of bad smells a day".
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Perhaps befitting Silicon Valley, the community is putting its hopes in technology.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered by local authorities to use drones and install monitors to systematically track and measure the chemicals responsible for bad odours.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: They have also been told to automate the collection of landfill gases responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Kong is optimistic a data-driven approach will make a difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Hopefully with this continuous monitoring, it makes it easier to pinpoint problems at the moment it starts." The operators of the landfill say they are committed to operating it safely and protecting air quality.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Just like in Milpitas, where Kong is part of a citizen's campaign against the odours, communities around the world are raising a stink about bad smells making day-to-day life miserable.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Sometimes a rubbish dump is to blame, or it might be a sewage treatment works, or a reeking factory.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: When the complaints start stacking up, resolving them is not always simple.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Urban sprawl is often part of the problem, bringing communities closer to stinky facilities that may historically have been kept at a distance.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This is creating more demand for technologies to monitor and prevent smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour consultant Micheal Bull says people are increasingly concerned about neighbourhood stinks.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "You're getting developments being built nearer to odorous processes… as land has become more valuable, there is also infilling," Bull says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: He is speaking about his experiences in the UK, but it's a similar story in many parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites are among the most difficult to resolve The technologies used to tackle industrial pongs generally fall into three categories: they absorb odours; convert them into something less smelly through a chemical reaction; or burn them away.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Experts on fixing industrial odours say that the best technologies, when used correctly, can remove 90% or more of the target compounds responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But this can be expensive and some operators opt for simpler and cheaper solutions.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: These include masking odours from landfill or sewage processing by spraying giant quantities of deodorisers.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour experts contacted for this article were dubious about the effectiveness of such industrial scale air fresheners.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "In my view they're not likely to change the odours," says Bull, who likens them to fabric conditioner.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites – a common cause of complaints – are among the stinkiest and most difficult to resolve, according to Carlos Diaz, an environmental consultant based in Spain.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Landfill is difficult to treat because you have a very large surface," he says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In some places at least, technology is making a real difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Residents in Des Moines, Iowa, have long complained of the so-called Eastside Funk, a putrid scent that residents report drifts over parts of the city.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: A study commissioned by city authorities showed that a trio of industrial meat companies were among culprits.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Within 10 miles, there's about half a million people," says Dalton Jacobus, who works in the Department of Neighborhood Services.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "If the winds are out of the wrong direction, 100,000 people can be in the middle of that odour plume." The authorities are now paying around $240,000 (£182,000) a year on technology to track the stink, so they can take action.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "What we wanted to do was build a ring of odour monitors around the facilities that we suspected of emitting odours," says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The monitors, which measure levels of chemical compounds in the air, work in combination with a weather station to provide real-time data on the concentrations that are coming from each facility based off the wind patterns.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This has put an end to finger pointing about who's to blame each time a smell sparks complaints, says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Smithfield Foods, which operates a meat processing in Des Moines, says it has invested $2m to install a regenerative thermal oxidiser that destroys the chemicals associated with bad smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Even so, the company says it does not believe it is the source of odour complaints.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Before installing the monitors – which some local companies help pay for – officials in Des Moines would drive out to the source of a complaint to sniff the air.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Relying on the human nose to sniff out industrial smells is still commonplace.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Claudia Barrios Obregón from Kunak, the company behind the monitors in Des Moines, says: "Right now, the way that cities control or measure odours is olfactometry: a human panel measures and gives an opinion of what the odour is like.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But that's not that realistic." The Spanish company's monitors are an example of so-called electronic noses that make it easier to detect smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Whatever technology is used, it can be hard to keep everyone happy, as smells are so subjective.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, the general rule is that the nastier we perceive the odour to be, the more sensitive towards it we are," says Johan Lundström, a professor in the science of smell at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm, Sweden.

sentences.text: Crime scene evidence is often not enough to identify suspects Randy Gail Sperino was last seen alive on the evening of 9 November 1993, as she was getting into a pickup truck in Granite City, Illinois.

sentences.text: The 34-year-old's body was found hours later in a field nearby, the victim of blunt force trauma.

sentences.text: The identity of her killer was a mystery.

sentences.text: DNA evidence found at the crime scene was tested against standard law enforcement databases, but no matches were found.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: For three decades, investigators from the Madison County Sheriff's Office chased leads and interviewed hundreds of people as they attempted to identify the perpetrator.

sentences.text: The case looked like it would remain one of more than 250,000 unsolved homicides in the US.

sentences.text: Then, last year, detectives tried a fresh approach.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They sent genetic evidence to Othram, a Houston-based company that uses DNA technology to help identify the perpetrators in cold and current crime cases.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The Madison County detectives had been inspired by investigative genetic genealogy techniques used to identify the Golden State Killer, Joseph James DeAngelo, back in 2018.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: In that case, an investigative team constructed a family tree to help identify the killer.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They were able to do so thanks to DNA data that relatives had provided to commercial databases, similar to consumer ancestry platforms.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Unlike traditional forensic DNA testing, which generally relies on a direct comparison between evidence and a known person, investigative genetic genealogy can identify distant genetic relatives of an unknown individual.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Othram set about applying this technique to track down Sperino's killer.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: While the suspect's own DNA profile wasn't available, profiles submitted by his extended relatives allowed the company to identify a male family member.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: "That lead broke the case open," said Captain Tim Lawrence of Madison County Sheriff's Office, which was responsible for investigating the crime.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: It was a crucial clue that led the detectives to Albert "Buddy" Zigler, 70, who police say then confessed to the murder.

sentences.text: He was charged in May this year.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Wes Sperino, Gail's son, said at a press conference: "I finally get closure and I finally know who did this." Albert Zigler was charged with murder in May The technique that led detectives to Zigler is credited with revolutionising how forensic cases are solved.

sentences.text: It has been highly successful in helping solve cases involving unidentified human remains and identifying suspects in longstanding investigations.

sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The Speaker of the House of Commons has expressed "frustration" with the lack of progress on restoration to protect the Palace of Westminster.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: Sir Lindsay Hoyle told the BBC the current process for approving essential renovations to Parliament amounted to "putting ourselves in handcuffs", and said more time was spent "doing surveys" than getting repairs under way.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: The Commons public accounts committee this week warned it was "crunch time" for the ailing building's restoration, which could cost up to £40bn and take 61 years.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: It said every additional year of delay cost taxpayers £420m, while its chairman warned the Palace could be left vulnerable to a devastating fire like that which engulfed the Notre Dame.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: Sir Lindsay said his "biggest frustration" with the Victorian building's restoration was that "we're not getting on with the work".
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: "We spend more time doing surveys," he told BBC Radio 4's The Week in Westminster .
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: "Instead of doing surveys, why don't we start repairing the building?" The Speaker criticised current legislation which means the main renovations cannot begin until Parliament has approved the entire project's scope and funding.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: "It's very frustrating when the Act of Parliament prevents you carrying out the major repairs that you need to.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: "The major part and the most historic parts of the building haven't got it, and that's what we need." Asked about reports that Parliament might be given an opportunity to vote on the way forward before the end of 2026, Sir Lindsay said that was a matter for government business managers.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: "Who knows when it's going to come forward?
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: Let's see what the House decides," he said.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: Fire safety issues and high levels of asbestos have also been identified.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: Kieran Kyle said Kemi Badenoch would get "a bullet in her head" if she went to Belfast, the court heard A man has been jailed for sending the Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch emails threatening to shoot her dead.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: Ex-teacher Kieran Kyle sent three emails on 2 May to the Tory party leader in which he made racist references and claimed to have been in the IRA, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: The 43-year-old, from Gillingham in Kent, pleaded guilty on 22 September at Westminster Magistrates' Court to two counts of sending communications of an indecent or offensive nature.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: Kyle was sentenced to 20 weeks in prison at the same court on Monday.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: In a victim impact statement read to the court, Badenoch and her husband Hamish said the "malicious communications and targeted harassment" not only had an effect on them, but also undermined "a healthy democracy".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: In two of the emails, Kyle had made racist references and written: "I'm ex-IRA, so Bloody Sunday references from you are going to give you trouble," the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: The messages were sent on the day Badenoch apologised for footage from Bloody Sunday being mistakenly used in a social media clip to criticise a parliamentary Bill on legacy issues in Northern Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: The Tory leader had said she did not sign off the video and that it was sent out by "very young people".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: The video criticising the Northern Ireland Troubles Bill, posted to her social media channels on 28 April, showed Badenoch saying the Labour legislation would "drag" Troubles veterans back to court.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: Thirteen unarmed civilians were shot dead when members of the Army's Parachute Regiment opened fire on civil rights demonstrators in the Bogside area of Londonderry on 30 January 1972, a date that became known as Bloody Sunday.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: The court heard Kyle had also sent an email to Badenoch's husband Hamish on 29 April, which used a racist term and said she had a "big mouth" and he should "put a leash on her".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: The Tory leader was said to have been left upset and distressed by the messages Prosecutor Ben Holt said the North West Essex MP and her husband were left "distressed" and "upset", particularly by the "racist language and threats of violence used towards them".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: He added Cheryl Bacon, head of Badenoch's parliamentary office, said the emails were "disgusting" and "distressing" to read.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: Baiju Thittala, defending, told the court Kyle "did not know" who Badenoch was at the time of the offences, adding "he only realised later, once he had sent the emails".
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: Asked by the judge how Kyle, a former secondary school teacher, could not know who Badenoch was, Thittala said: "He just 'Googled' it and it came up as the opposition leader." The judge said: "The first emails were sent to Mr Badenoch, so I don't think he did not appreciate who Mrs Badenoch was.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: "When individuals choose to intimidate, threaten, or aggressively target elected representatives or public figures, the harm extends far beyond any single person.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: It undermines a healthy democracy." The continued: "Public service relies on people being willing to step forward, often at significant personal cost, to represent their communities and contribute to public life.
sentences.article_title: Man jailed over racist Badenoch death threats

sentences.text: "Increasingly, however, those who do so face hostility, harassment, and attempts to silence or intimidate them." The judge also handed Kyle a restraining order, meaning he cannot contact Badenoch, her husband or her parliamentary office for five years.

sentences.text: New blood tests designed to check for multiple cancers in one go will be offered to NHS patients in some 200 GP surgeries in England as part of a trial.

sentences.text: These cancers are often found only after they have spread.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The walkout will begin on 25 November at 06:59 GMT, with consultants staffing emergency care only.

sentences.text: This is known as Christmas Day cover and is likely to have a major impact on most routine and elective or planned services.

sentences.text: The announcement comes after talks had been taking place with the government over the past month, following the vote in favour of strike action by British Medical Association members in July.

sentences.text: Consultants – the most senior doctors in hospitals – were given a 3.5% pay increase this year.

sentences.text: But the BMA argues pay has fallen by a quarter over the past 17 years, once inflation is taken into account.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The union also wants a reduction in the standard working week, from 40 to 35 hours, and higher pay for out-of-hours work, alongside changes to pensions, including greater flexibility over when they can be taken.

sentences.text: In a joint statement, BMA consultants committee co-chairs Dr Helen Neary and Dr Shanu Datta, said they had tried to negotiate with the government in "good faith", but "time-and-time again ministers have kicked the can down the road".

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, that road has now run out, and we have been forced to announce strikes.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: "My low Vitamin D levels hit me like a truck" Twenty-three-year-old Saskia Reeves-Priestley was at work when she suddenly collapsed.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I just felt really dizzy, really nauseous, was having heart palpitations and was really hot," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Saskia, a special educational needs teacher, was a keen goalkeeper who played football four times a week and felt fit and healthy.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: While her symptoms are not directly linked to vitamin D deficiency - she realised something was wrong.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Blood tests later showed her level was so low - it was "next to nothing".
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In the UK, low vitamin D rates are increasing in some age groups , external - particularly in girls and young women.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: According to data from the National Diet and Nutrition Survey, last year nearly a quarter of 11- to 18-year-olds were classed as deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D can come from our diet, in foods such as oily fish and meat, or supplements.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: But most is made by our body when UV light in sunlight hits the skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Lower levels of sunlight - depending on where in the world you live or the time of year - decrease the body's ability to produce it.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Covering parts of the body and wearing sunscreen also has an impact - despite their protective advantages.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Those with darker skin need exposure to stronger light to produce the same amount of vitamin D as lighter skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Doctors don't routinely offer blood tests to check for vitamin D deficiency, but will offer a supplement if a patient is concerned they might be high risk.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D deficiency is linked to the bone disease rickets in babies and infants.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In adults it causes a similar weakening of the bone called osteomalacia , external .
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "They call it the silent disease," says Dr Suma Uday, a paediatric endocrinologist who wants to raise awareness of the problem.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: She warns that vitamin D deficiency in young people and adults is difficult to spot and can be missed or misdiagnosed.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Symptoms include fatigue and joint and bone pain.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Uday says: "It's basically silently eating away at the bones, leaving them softened and prone to breaks." Amaka Osu says she doesn't think many of her friends realise what the symptoms are Amaka was in the middle of making dinner at her university house in Liverpool when she started shaking.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I couldn't really see in front of me," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Her housemate took her to A&E - later she too would be diagnosed as vitamin D deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Other than feeling tired, she says she had no symptoms: "I'm a 21-year-old student.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: I've got work and uni - I'm always feeling tired." She remembers her mother suffering from low vitamin D but says she did not realise it could happen to her.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: After taking supplements, Amaka feels a lot better, but she is anxious in case it happens again.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "It was scary and I don't want to experience that again." Uday joins other clinicians and academics who have formed a group - ACT NOW Vitamin D - calling for the threshold at which you are classified as deficient to be raised.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: She says that would "catch" more people with low vitamin D and give a more accurate picture of how widespread the issue is.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: It would also mean they can treat the deficiency earlier, she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Uday warns of "a lifelong deficit" in women - in adolescence, then pregnancy, and then the newborn is affected.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "If you don't correct it from the very beginning," she says, "this is going to affect multiple generations." Saskia Reeves-Priestley plays football four times a week - and had no previous symptoms "It's shocking," says Prof Martin Hewison, from the University of Birmingham.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: He tells me that despite being 100 years on from the discovery of vitamin D "rickets hasn't gone away".
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "If we have rickets in the community, there are going to be many more people who are vitamin D deficient." He says the government should look into wider fortification of food in which vitamins are added to foods during production.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Countries like Canada and Sweden have mandatory policies.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In the UK, some foods such as breakfast cereals and spreads are already fortified with vitamin D, but it is voluntary.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: During the winter months, people start to lose their vitamin D levels.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "We might have to accept that for certain groups vitamin D supplementation is a matter of course," says Hewison.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Saskia is now taking vitamin D supplements regularly - and is back in goal.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: "However, it may be a clue to tell us that something is going on." Pale skin, hair shedding or brittle nails can accompany low iron, but can also be signs of other conditions, she told BBC News.

sentences.article_title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?

sentences.text: Stockpiles of blood have dropped below required levels due to falling donor numbers An amber alert has come into force for the first time as stocks of blood in Scotland have dropped to unprecedented low levels due to the shortage of donors.

sentences.text: The warning has been sent to hospitals across the country by the Scottish National Blood Transfusion Service (SNBTS), urging medical staff to only use Type O blood when essential.

sentences.text: Type O blood is particularly important for transfusions as O-negative acts as a universal donor and O-positive is the most common blood type in the UK, with about 35% of the population having it.

sentences.text: Stocks have consistently been below target levels for several weeks and Group O blood has fallen to below two days of reserves on several occasions recently.

sentences.text: Dr Afifa Qazi from Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust said the opening was an important step forward The first NHS intensive care unit for women with serious mental health needs in Kent and Medway is due to open.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: Women in the region will have access to a dedicated NHS psychiatric intensive care unit for the first time, following a £4.63m investment by Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: The 10-bed facility at Littlestone Lodge in Dartford will provide short-term, intensive care for women experiencing serious mental health difficulties who need extra support.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: Dr Afifa Qazi, chief medical officer for the trust, said the opening was an important step forward and that until now women needing intensive care and support "have not been able to receive this specialist care from our team".
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: The unit is expected to provide around 2,500 bed days of care for women each year, and is due to welcome its first patient towards the end of November.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: Qazi said: "This new service means we can now provide specialist, compassionate care at a particularly difficult time in their lives.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: Two of the 10 beds will also be available to women referred by other NHS trusts, depending on individual needs.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: The trust already provides intensive mental health care for men at Willow Suite, a 12-bed unit at Littlebrook Hospital.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: The new unit extends this specialist service to women.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: The unit is expected to provide around 2,500 bed days of care for women each year.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: People with personal experience of mental health services helped shape the unit, and its design also takes account of sensory needs, including those of women with autism and learning disabilities.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: Jim Dickson, MP for Dartford, said women experiencing serious mental health difficulties deserved "care that treats them with dignity, compassion and an understanding of their individual needs".
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: "I'm pleased to see this new unit open in Dartford.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: It is an important investment in mental health services for women and their families across Kent and Medway," he said.

sentences.text: The government has warned some schools start teaching GCSEs in the first year of secondary school Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught in England.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The government plans to make Key Stage 3 a more distinct education phase, urging schools to focus less on exams and more on a "richer, more engaging" experience.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The changes come in response to two reviews that found pupils were increasingly becoming disengaged in their early teenage years, affecting attendance and achievement, the Department for Education (DfE) said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The move will mark a reversal of the approach taken by the previous Conservative government to focus the first three years of secondary school on core subjects and on doing well in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Former Education Secretary Michael Gove prioritised English, maths and science, while raising grade boundaries, making exams harder and limiting resits.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: He also made GCSEs linear, meaning they are sat all in one go at the end of Year 11 instead of over the course of Key Stage 4.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: These reforms meant teachers started preparing pupils for exams at an earlier stage at the expense of teaching unexamined parts of their subject.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The DfE has pledged a "more engaging offer" in subjects like drama, PE, music and languages, which have seen a decline in students taking them, when it publishes its new curriculum later this year.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: It says persistent absence nearly doubles among pupils between Year 6 and Year 9.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The department pointed to a recent survey commissioned by the International Baccalaureate that found GCSE prep dominated Key Stage 3 learning in England, with 57% of teachers saying it was the leading influence on the curriculum.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "The pressures of GCSEs and an overcrowded curriculum are resulting in too many children receiving a narrower offer during Key Stage 3 and being rushed towards exams without grasping the fundamentals or developing deeper understanding," Powell said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "I'm putting a stop to that." A 2015 Ofsted report suggested that Key Stage 3 may be "wasted years", echoing the view at the time that pupils aged 11-14 lacked a clear motivation to work hard.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: However, the government faced criticism at the time that its reforms made each exam far more significant, meaning teachers refocused lessons only on what could come up in them.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: She added that a new curriculum "alone won't get children back into the classroom", noting that "too many pupils are missing school because of anxiety and unmet mental health needs" while "schools can't offer more drama, music and languages without the teachers to teach them".

sentences.text: Several universities in England have only been using below-average salaries in examples of student loan repayments on their websites, the BBC has found.

sentences.text: Treasury Committee chair Dame Meg Hillier, who led a recent inquiry into student loans, said some information about repayments was "misleading", including one instance where they were compared to the "cost of a daily coffee".

sentences.text: Student loan repayments are tied to earnings, so the more you earn, the more you repay every month - and graduates generally go on to earn more than non-graduates.

sentences.text: Current and prospective students in England take out Plan 5 loans to pay for their tuition fees and living costs.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The BBC looked at publicly available information on more than 110 university websites in England and found cases of inaccurate information about the salary at which they start repaying and the length of time they repay for.

sentences.article_title: 'My brother died, so I smashed up his TV'

sentences.article_title: 'My brother died, so I smashed up his TV'

sentences.text: Concerns have been raised with the government about the amount of time primary school children are spending on a game designed to make learning times tables fun.

sentences.text: TT Rockstars, which allows children to compete with their classmates for virtual coins and rock-star themed characters and outfits, is widely used by schools for maths homework.
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

sentences.text: Labour MP Emily Darlington said the app and others like it could be harming children's development because it rewards them for "length of time rather than quality of time spent online".
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

sentences.text: Bruno Reddy, founder of the firm behind TT Rockstars, said he shared concerns about screen time and was working with schools to bring in curfews and time limits.
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

sentences.text: He said the company discourages long sessions, adding: "Every game in TTRS is deliberately short, and our characters remind children to take regular breaks.
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

sentences.text: "The rule of thumb we give schools is: three minutes, four or five times a week.
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

sentences.text: In September, a typical child played on three days, for about six minutes each time." He said that from 24 November "every school will have a curfew and a daily time limit switched on, and leaderboards switched off as default".
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

sentences.text: Darlington told BBC News that while education technology, or EdTech, can have a place in the classroom "when gamification is used, children spend hours online to 'earn' the latest outfit".
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

sentences.text: "Parents are concerned that this causes conflict on time spent on devices and the pressure to perform against classmates," she added, and this could deter them from taking part in real life, rather than screen-based, activities.

sentences.text: The Milton Keynes Central MP raised concerns about TT Rockstars on Tuesday at the Commons Science Committee, which is investigating the impact of screen time and digital devices on children's brain development.

sentences.text: US Assistant Attorney General Colin M McDonald vowed to pursue all those involved In May 2024, Francis Mogambi arrived in the United States after winning the Diversity Visa lottery, a programme that gives people from around the world a chance to become permanent residents.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Just over two years later, the Kenyan national found himself at the centre of a US investigation into an alleged nationwide scheme to defraud the federal student aid system.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: On 19 October 2026, a grand jury in Nebraska indicted Mogambi on five counts of theft of government money and five counts of aggravated identity theft.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Prosecutors allege that, between November 2025 and May 2026, he worked with associates in Kenya to steal the identities of US citizens and use them to fraudulently enroll fictitious students in American colleges.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Once the fake students were enrolled, Mogambi allegedly diverted their financial aid payments to himself, keeping 30% and sending the remainder to his associates in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The intended loss in his case was $20,000 (£15,000), according to prosecutors.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Court documents say Mogambi received $2,000 a week and attempted to recruit another person into the scheme.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He allegedly told the individual he needed a business that would allow him to cash larger cheques without paying taxes.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Mogambi was arrested shortly after the indictment was returned and is being held in custody pending trial.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He has not yet commented on the allegations against him.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: His case forms part of a wider US investigation, dubbed Operation Ghostbusters, into the alleged use of stolen identities to enrol fictitious students at colleges and claim federal financial aid that resulted in a loss of $130m in taxpayers funds.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: US authorities say the investigation has so far resulted in five indictments that involved Kenyan nationals, while a further 40 investigations remain open.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Hundreds of people have been affected after fraudsters allegedly stole their personally identifiable information (PII) and used it to access federal student aid.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The stolen personal information was sometimes sold online for between $4 and $8, with fraudsters targeting low-income Americans who had never had the opportunity to attend college.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: At a news conference on 29 October announcing the first charges in the investigation, Assistant Attorney General Colin M McDonald, who heads the Justice Department's National Fraud Enforcement Division, vowed to pursue those involved.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "If you steal taxpayers' dollars, if you exploit a programme meant to help students, we are resolved to find you and prosecute you," he said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The Justice Department says those behind the fraud use what is described as "super intelligence" to place fake students in classrooms and complete coursework, creating the impression that they are attending college and allowing financial aid payments to continue.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "The goal is to keep the ghost student in school as long as possible.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Semester after semester after semester stealing money from the taxpayers," McDonald said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: But the consequences extend beyond the financial losses suffered by the US government.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: People whose identities are stolen can find themselves facing unexpected student loan debts, even if they have never enrolled in college.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "His identity was stolen, his credit is now at risk, and his name is on the bill," McDonald said, describing the impact on one victim.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He also said that nearly a third of community college applicants in California in 2024 had been identified as fraudulent.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The scale of the suspected fraud is significant.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Investigators identified 830,840 potentially fraudulent Federal Student Aid identification numbers associated with nearly $130m in September and October 2026.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: They recommended that the Department of Education disable them.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The figure represents financial aid associated with potentially fraudulent accounts, not confirmed losses.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "In a flash, the money vanishes, often overseas in places like Kenya," McDonald said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The investigation has also exposed alleged financial links between the US and Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: In September, US officials travelled to Kenya to work with local law enforcement on extraditions, prosecutions and the recovery of money allegedly stolen from American taxpayers.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: With the help of Kenyan investigators, US authorities seized more than $750,000  from a cryptocurrency account belonging to a Kenyan national connected to the wider scheme.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The Justice Department described it as the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The seizure was not connected to Mogambi's individual case.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: In a separate case in Virginia, prosecutors allege that a Kenyan national received more than 700 fraudulent student-aid refunds totalling approximately $1.44m.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: At least $1.3m was subsequently transferred through thousands of transactions to accounts in the US and Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Meanwhile, in New Jersey, three people have been charged with allegedly acting as money mules in a scheme to obtain more than $1m in federal student aid.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Prosecutors say they received the funds through US bank accounts, kept a portion for themselves and transferred the remainder to alleged co-conspirators in Kenya linked to a purported safari company.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Authorities say those convicted will also face appropriate orders for forfeiture of assets and restitution to victims, in addition to any prison sentences.

sentences.text: This video can not be played The zeptoverse explained by BBC science correspondent Pallab Ghosh Scientists have picked up signals from the smallest scale of nature ever explored – 100 billion times smaller than an atom.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: A world so small that some physicists have nicknamed it the zeptoverse.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: The research, led by scientists based in Cambridge, was obtained from an experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC).
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: This vast machine at the European Laboratory for Particle Physics (Cern) on the Swiss-French border smashes atoms together to break them apart and discover what is inside them.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: The result is important because it could help researchers develop a new, more complete theory of how the Universe works.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Many sub-atomic particles are created by smashing the insides of atoms together Dark matter makes up a large part of our cosmos, and yet researchers have struggled to detect it.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Scientists know it is there because its gravitational force influences normal matter, but in all other respects it has remained completely invisible.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: So in this experiment, particles were smashed together at high energy and scientists studied the material that was thrown out - the shrapnel of collisions.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: One of these is a sub-atomic particle - smaller than an atom - called a beauty quark.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: The particle is unstable and exists for just one and a half trillionths of a second before breaking down into other forms - decaying.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Despite its short lifetime, researchers managed to detect it interacting with other tiny particles at a scale of a billion-trillionth of a metre.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Some theories suggest that at these scales particles are more sensitive to dark matter and it could influence how the quarks interact and break down.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: So, detecting activity in this tiny world could help scientists detect dark matter.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: "We're knocking on the door of this zeptoverse," Dr Harry Cliff, of Cambridge University who led the analysis of the data, told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: He said this sub-atomic dance provided researchers with a ringside seat to the behaviour of possible new particles.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: "And what we want to do now is go in and explore and find what new particles are waiting there.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: And to do that, what we need is more data," Cliff added.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Dr Harry Cliff is one of a team of British scientists involved in the research The 28 countries involved in the project have agreed a £150m upgrade to this detector at the Large Hadron Collider (LHCb), which would increase the frequency of these decays tenfold.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: "With that we can probe inside the zeptoverse and see what's waiting," Cliff said.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: But last year the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) agency, the government body in charge of research funding, announced that it was withdrawing its share of the money for the planned upgrade.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: It later announced cuts to several other particle physics and astronomy projects this Summer, including Jodrell Bank's iconic Lovell telescope .
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Although this research was led by scientists based in Cambridge, because of the cuts, Prof Tim Gershon, who leads the LHCb international collaboration, told BBC News that the UK's full involvement in the research would be in doubt.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: "The UK is at risk of not being involved and making really major discoveries," he told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: She is reconsidering her future in light of the physics cuts.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: She added that "lots" of her fellow researchers working in fundamental physics had already moved.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: The cuts are being made despite an overall record increase in the science budget.

sentences.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was finally released on Thursday, after years of rumours that Nintendo would remake the game - considered one of the best ever made.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: IGN called it "the biggest game of the decade" in their review , external when it launched in 1998 on the N64, and it set the standard for 3D games.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: A lot of the things we take for granted in modern games - such as riding a horse, fighting with a sword and shield, or locking on to enemies with the tap of a button - were pioneered or perfected in Ocarina of Time.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: It received an almost perfect score from critics and, decades on, remains the highest-rated game in history on Metacritic, which aggregates reviews.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: So how do you remake what many consider a masterpiece?
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: This video can not be played WATCH: Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time - how the remake compares to the original Those like me who grew up playing the original will feel right at home here.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: Nintendo has decided against reinventing the wheel, instead producing something which plays very similarly to the N64 classic.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: As I've said before , video game remakes are a bit different to film or TV - gaming fans often clamour for a new take on their favourites, hoping developers harness evolution in tech to make them fresh.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: And games have come a long way in the almost 30 years since the original Ocarina of Time came out.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: "When you compare the games in the past and the games in modern times, so to speak, the norms of what people expect from a game have evolved naturally," Nintendo producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi told me.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: Some might even be disappointed by this, given the N64 game had quite horrifying elements in places.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: One was the Skulltula House, a room where people had been morphed into human-spider hybrids.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: "Back when we created the original Ocarina of Time, the means to convey or express ideas was limited compared with what we have now," series producer Eiji Aonuma - who worked on the original game - said.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: "With regard to even the so-called scary elements, we strove to add a touch of the comical." But he told the BBC that enhanced graphics and lighting capabilities unintentionally exaggerated the already-spooky Skulltula House and its potential to strike fear into players.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: "When we carried out the test play, the testers were telling us, 'Oh, this is too scary'," he said.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: "So of course, in the end product, we've made the necessary adjustments so that we can retain the same balance that we had achieved in the original." I spoke to a few YouTubers about the upcoming game to get their thoughts - and the response was overwhelmingly positive.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: Mike Channell, co-editor of the YouTube channel Outside Xbox, said he believed the remake had been made "very meticulously" in the hopes of living up to fan expectations.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: "Having played the game, it's clear that serious thought has gone into every decision, to the point where I'm not convinced this remake has taken any less time and effort than an all-new Zelda game," he said.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: "Ocarina of Time is obviously one of the great video game experiences in the history of the medium, but I have no doubt this new version will be the best way to experience this story.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: "The Forest Temple has always been my favourite Zelda dungeon: a mysterious, haunted mansion in the deep woods, a lost work of man slowly being reclaimed by nature," he said.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: "The remake really leans into the surreal, uncanny nature of the original dungeon." And fellow YouTuber StrawHatMidas said it was the "perfect" way to "bring this classic back".
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: "Not only does the game pay homage to the Nintendo 64 original, but it also expands on the things that made it so memorable," he said.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: "Everything from the world and atmosphere to the controls and soundtrack feels like a love letter to the classic Zelda formula." Nintendo has made some big changes, not least to the Water Temple - a dungeon about two thirds into the game.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: Aonuma said, having worked on the original, this was what he personally wanted to change most due to its reputation for being "very, very difficult".
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: He said there was now "a greater facility in tackling" the dungeon, as players can now easily change a critical in-game item known as heavy boots and have "the ability to leverage the camera orientation".
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: I grew up playing Zelda on the N64, which pioneered the joystick - but nowadays two sticks is the standard, with one to move and one to control the camera.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: As far as I'm concerned, being able to freely move the camera this time round was a significant improvement.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: Link's fingers now move over the holes of the ocarina as he plays At times, the trip down memory lane was captivating.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: I knew where to go and what to do, thanks to a kind of muscle memory.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: However, on occasion that took away from the experience - with some tasks achieved too easily and some puzzles too quickly because I recalled their solutions.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: Some people will love how similar it is, but I have to wonder if Nintendo has played things a bit too safe.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: I don't think the developers see it that way.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: "Even if the game may look different, we've maintained the essence that the original developers wanted to and hopefully conveyed through the original Ocarina of Time," Fujibayashi said.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: Don't get me wrong - the game has lots of changes and surprises, and I won't spoil them, but I wish there had been more.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: Then again, perhaps the best games leave you wanting more.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: Or as Mike put it: "I loved the original as much as the next person, but I don't think I'll be going back to it." Fans will no doubt wonder whether this is it, or if there will be more Zelda on the horizon.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: With the franchise's first movie coming next year, there's certainly more to come in the short term.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: And in the long term, I wondered if with 30 more years of technological advancements, Nintendo might consider remaking the game once again.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: "I will be long retired," Aonuma said, with a laugh.
sentences.article_title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?

sentences.text: Michael Ball attended Dave and Dawn Lloyd's wedding ceremony on Sunday A couple whose surprise radio proposal captured hearts across the country were given an unforgettable wedding gift when singer and broadcaster Michael Ball turned up to perform at their ceremony.

sentences.text: Dawn Lloyd was shocked when her partner of more than 25 years Dave proposed on BBC Radio 2's Love Songs with Michael Ball programme in the summer and was stunned all over again when the presenter appeared at the couple's wedding at Weston Hall, in Stafford, on Sunday.

sentences.text: "I had no inkling whatsoever that this was going to happen," she said.

sentences.text: "I just can't believe Dave has surprised me like this a second time.

sentences.text: This video can not be played 'I wanted to prove that motherhood is not the finish line' - ultrarunner Stephanie Case Ultra-runner Stephanie Case has made history by becoming the first woman to complete an extreme 100-mile race in Antarctica.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: The Antarctic Ice Ultra consists of 38 loops of a 4.2km course in the Schirmacher Oasis in Queen Maud Land, East Antarctica.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: The 43-year-old ran alongside penguins and battled severe wind and temperatures as low as -35C - the coldest organisers have ever seen - to cross the finish line in second place overall in a time of 17 hours 31 minutes and 39 seconds.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: Due to the harsh weather conditions, the race was brought forward to start at 1am on Sunday morning and Case says it was as much about survival as performance.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: "When you're out in that environment for 20 minutes it's OK but when you're out in it for 17 hours or more, it can take a huge toll on the body because you have to expend so much energy just to keep yourself warm," Case told BBC Sport.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: "The thing is that you need to run fast, but you need to do it in a way that you don't sweat, because if you sweat, that's a killer.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: It will make you cold instantly." Stephanie Case is the first woman in history to run 100 miles on Antarctica Such is the brutal nature of the challenge on a continent that has 24/7 daylight,  very few people attempt it each year and even fewer finish.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: This year, only four of the eight runners that started the 100-mile race crossed the finish line.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: Previously only ever attempted by men, Case was one of three women on the start line but the Canadian was the only one to finish.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: One of the challenges Case had not considered though, as a self-declared "mountain goat", was managing toilet breaks in the extreme temperatures.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: "On a trail you could normally just go in the woods, but due to bio-security reasons, you can't leave any trace in Antarctica.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: And then going to the bathroom, when you are wearing so many layers and taking off your gloves for even five seconds can put your hands at risk of frostbite, it was a real challenge," she said.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: "The environment is so harsh, and things can go wrong so quickly… It was just relief when I crossed the finish line that I'd actually done it and in a time that I was super proud of.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: It was just an outpouring of emotion." The runners battled temperatures as low as -35C The human rights lawyer crossed the line 29 minutes after Chinese runner Yusheng Ni, who smashed his own world record - set last year - by over five and a half hours.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: Alongside making history, Case had also been chasing the world record but knew she would have a "formidable challenge" on her hands with Ni, who has completed more than 500 ultramarathons, in the pack.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: "There were parts where I was 60 seconds behind him or I was sometimes just 200 metres behind him.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: But whenever he saw me getting close, he would look behind and he would just take off.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: I think we really pushed each other to get our best performances.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: I feel super proud of what I was able to do," she said.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: Case went viral last year for breastfeeding her baby daughter Pepper during her victory at an ultramarathon in Snowdonia.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: While the response was largely positive, she says some of the backlash she received is what inspired her to take on this challenge to show "motherhood is not the finish line".
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: To do it in a place that has historically been described as the "womanless continent", she says, is a fitting achievement.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: "I know that when I'm going out and doing the things that make me feel happy and whole, it makes me a better mum and I can come home and and show my daughter all the things that she might want to do and all the things that are possible for women," Case said.
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: "I felt like the best way to clap back at anyone who thought that I should be at home with my baby was to go to the most extreme place on Earth and try to get the record." Are women better than men at endurance running?
sentences.article_title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica

sentences.text: England Netball is among the organisations to back the Equal Sport Project The English Football Association, Team GB and England Netball are among major organisations to back the Equal Sport Project - a new initiative aimed at improving equality and making the UK world leaders for women and girls' sport.
sentences.article_title: Initiative launched to make UK world leader in women's sport

sentences.text: Recent research by Sporting Insights found that fewer than 1% of women working in sport believe gender equality has been achieved across the industry, while more than half believe they are paid less than men for carrying out the same role.
sentences.article_title: Initiative launched to make UK world leader in women's sport

sentences.text: Consequently, the Equal Sport Project has identified five areas where improved leadership, investment and action will have the greatest impact in bringing equality for women and men across sport.
sentences.article_title: Initiative launched to make UK world leader in women's sport

sentences.text: The Youth Sport Trust, meanwhile, has committed to support schools in recognising and challenging stereotypes as well as develop male allies to champion gender equality in PE, school sport and physical activity.
sentences.article_title: Initiative launched to make UK world leader in women's sport

sentences.text: The project is also backed by the UK government, with sports minister Stephanie Peacock saying: "We have seen progress in women and girls' sport, but there is still a long way to go.
sentences.article_title: Initiative launched to make UK world leader in women's sport

sentences.text: "We will work closely with the Equal Sport Project and encourage all organisations to get involved.
sentences.article_title: Initiative launched to make UK world leader in women's sport

sentences.text: Together we can make the UK a world leader in women and girls' sport."
